Method of Attack: Distributed via SPAM emails targeting Danish victims with fake invoice emails containing a link to a malicious Word document
Malicious Word document tricks user into enabling macros which download and install the ransomware
Copies itself to a random folder under %AppData%, connects to ipinfo.io to check victim's IP and country
Exits without encrypting if victim is from certain countries (Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Russia, Turkmenistan, Tajikistan)
Connects to Command & Control server to send victim info and receive RSA public key
Terminates database-related processes to unlock files
Encrypts files with AES-256, appends encrypted AES key with RSA key, appends .serpent extension
Clears Windows Volume Shadow Copies and overwrites deleted data with cipher.exe
Creates VBS autorun file in Startup folder for persistence
Drops ransom notes with payment instructions and links to payment site
Impacted Systems: Windows computers with database-related processes running
Attack Vector: SPAM emails with malicious Word document containing macros

Malicious Word document prompting to enable macros
